item.title: Tyreek Hill's NFL return seemed imminent and then his divorce trial began with domestic abuse allegations
item.description: Tyreek Hill's estranged wife testified during divorce proceedings he tried to punch her stomach while pregnant, allegations that could delay NFL return.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple reports that surfaced recently linked Tyreek Hill to a Kansas City Chiefs return and one report even quoted his agent as saying he expected the former All-Pro wide receiver to sign with a team in the coming days. That's before Hill's divorce trial began Tuesday.

And testimony from Lakeeta Vaccaro, the player's estranged wife, outlined incidents of domestic abuse. Her suit complaint outlined eight instances of abuse.

The divorce itself is of no interest to the NFL. But the allegations of abuse definitely are and could derail or at least significantly delay Hill's return to the field under the league's Personal Conduct Policy.

NFL FACES DOMESTIC ABUSE EPIDEMIC THIS OFFSEASON

Hill is a free agent but the NFL review of his domestic violence allegations by Vaccaro is ongoing with no timetable for a conclusion, a league source confirmed to OutKick.

Tuesday's accounting of those allegations in open court almost definitely will be taken into account as part of that review that will determine Hill's status to play when healthy.

RAVENS' RASHOD BATEMAN FACES DOMESTIC CHARGES FOR ALLEGED ATTACK ON CAR CARRYING EX-GIRLFRIEND AND THEIR BABY

Vaccaro, who is suing Hill for punitive and compensatory damages, testified during direct examination that in July 2024, she and Hill visited the ESPN campus in Orlando.

Vaccaro said Hill became upset because she did not get professional hair and makeup done for potential interviews there.

Later, at their hotel, Hill remained upset and became so heated he tried to punch her stomach, Vaccaro testified. She said she blocked the blow by putting her hands on her stomach, but the strike did hit her hands.

Vaccaro was pregnant at the time.

Vaccaro added that Hill told her that he didn’t want the baby.

Vaccaro, the sister of former NFL safety Kenny Vaccaro, alleged a history of abuse during her time with Hill. Their 18-month marriage, she testified, was punctuated by periods of relative peace followed by trouble.

"During this whole period, 18-month marriage, it was a consistent two-week on, two-week off situation," Vaccaro testified. "Of course we had our moments when it was, you know, beautiful.

"But then the two weeks of, when it went back to this angry man, it was bad."

Vaccaro said Hill once picked her up physically to throw her out of their house. She said he once pushed her into a car door during an argument. She accused Hill of grabbing and hurting her breasts during multiple arguments.

She accused Hill of once leaving her on the side of a road after an argument in their car.

Hill’s counsel tried to establish discrepancies between Vaccaro's deposition and her testimony on Tuesday and pressed the point no physical evidence of abuse exists. And Hill's lawyer said that while the allegations are serious, taking them seriously does not mean accepting them merely because they were made.

Hill has a history of alleged or proven abuse against women:

TYREEK HILL ACCUSED BY 250-POUND ONLYFANS MODEL OF BREAKING HER LEG, THEN GIVING HER A PIGGYBACK RIDE TO SEX

Tuesday’s proceedings wrapped up just after 5 p.m. and neither Hill nor Vaccaro spoke with reporters afterward.

The trial is scheduled to continue on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump says Putin call coming ‘very soon’ as US tracks suspected plague death in Russia
item.description: President Donald Trump says he'll speak with Vladimir Putin "very soon" as his administration tracks a suspected pneumonic plague death in Siberia.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Tuesday he will speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin "very soon" as his administration closely tracks reports of a suspected pneumonic plague death in Siberia that have prompted a U.S. health alert and heightened health precautions across several countries bordering Russia.

Trump revealed the planned call while taking questions from reporters Tuesday.

Asked whether he had spoken with Putin about the situation, Trump said he already had a call scheduled.

"I have a call scheduled, yup," Trump said.

TRUMP RESPONDS TO CONCERNS OVER SUSPECTED PLAGUE CASE IN RUSSIA, SAYING US 'WILLING TO HELP'

Asked when the call would take place, the president responded, "Very soon."

Trump said the administration was in "very deep discussions" when asked what U.S. intelligence agencies were saying about the reports.

The president's comments came as the U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a health alert Tuesday saying it was aware of press reports from Russia's Irkutsk region of "suspected pneumonic plague resulting in the death of an individual," along with associated quarantine measures and hospital closures.

"We continue to track the situation closely," the embassy said.

NEW YORK DECLARES MEASLES DISASTER EMERGENCY AS CASES SURGE IN PENNSYLVANIA

A State Department spokesman told Fox News Digital that the department, along with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and other interagency partners, is "closely monitoring the fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague" in Russia's Irkutsk Oblast.

"The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," the spokesman said.

The spokesman cautioned that "many details remain unconfirmed" and called on Moscow to provide greater clarity.

"We encourage Russian authorities to share accurate information quickly and openly," the spokesman said.

The alert advised Americans in the area to follow local health guidance, avoid affected medical facilities and seek prompt medical care if they develop fever or respiratory symptoms. Those who have traveled to an area experiencing an outbreak were advised to monitor their health for 14 days.

The State Department's existing Level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory for Russia remains unchanged. The embassy reiterated that Americans currently in Russia should depart and warned that the U.S. government's ability to assist citizens there is limited, particularly outside Moscow.

UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

Several countries bordering Russia are also implementing new health precautions in response to the reports.

Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan are moving to implement what their governments have described as "enhanced health and sanitary measures" in response to reports of pneumonic plague in Siberia.

A 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died last week from what Russian authorities described as pneumonia of undetermined origin. Russia has not said the woman died of plague and said testing found no microorganisms in her body linked to her work.

Russian officials told the WHO that her contacts tested negative for dangerous infectious pathogens. The WHO has assessed the risk to the general population as low.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has also said it is closely monitoring the reports and working across the U.S. government as additional information becomes available. The agency said there is currently no indication of a broader threat to the United States.

Pneumonic plague is a serious bacterial infection caused by Yersinia pestis. It can spread between people through respiratory droplets during close contact and can progress rapidly if untreated. The disease can be successfully treated with antibiotics, particularly when identified and treated early.

For now, U.S. officials are continuing to seek additional information about what occurred in Irkutsk and whether the incident poses any wider threat.

The president suggested his administration could have more to say as soon as Wednesday.

"We'll be able to report about it probably tomorrow," Trump said.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar-winning ‘On the Waterfront’ and ‘North by Northwest’ star, dead at 102
item.description: Oscar winning actress Eva Marie Saint, who starred opposite Marlon Brando and Cary Grant, has died at 102 after a career spanning seven decades.
item.content:encoded:
Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-and Emmy-winning actress who became one of the defining stars of Hollywood’s Golden Era, has died. She was 102.

Saint died Tuesday of natural causes at her Los Angeles home surrounded by family and loved ones, her representative confirmed to Fox News Digital.

The actress made an extraordinary film debut opposite Marlon Brando in the 1954 classic "On the Waterfront," winning the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress in her performance as Edie Doyle.

POST MALONE, EVA MARIE SAINT AND OTHER CELEBRITIES WHO SHARE A BIRTHDAY WITH THE FOURTH OF JULY

Five years later, Saint then firmly cemented her place in Hollywood's Golden Era history while starring opposite the legendary Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock’s "North by Northwest," playing mysterious "Hitchcock Blonde" Eve Kendall in the cult-classic 1959 thriller.

Over an incredible career spanning more than seven decades, Saint worked alongside some of Hollywood’s most celebrated leading men, including Montgomery Clift, Henry Fonda, Paul Newman, Gregory Peck, Richard Burton, Warren Beatty, James Garner, George C. Scott, Burt Lancaster and Tom Hanks.

OSCAR-WINNER BRENDA FRICKER, 'PIGEON LADY' FROM 'HOME ALONE 2,' DEAD AT 81

Other notable films featuring the actress included "A Hatful of Rain," "Raintree County," "Exodus," "The Russians Are Coming the Russians Are Coming," "Grand Prix," "Nothing in Common" and, later in her career, "Superman Returns."

Saint was also a regular fixture of television and the stage. She earned five Emmy nominations, winning in 1990 for the miniseries "People Like Us," and appeared on Broadway in "The Trip to Bountiful" before director Elia Kazan cast her in "On the Waterfront."

SHELLEY FABARES, STAR OF 'THE DONNA REED SHOW' AND 'COACH,' DEAD AT 82

Born in Newark, New Jersey, and raised in Albany and Delmar, New York, Saint attended Bowling Green State University in Ohio with plans to become a teacher before acting ultimately changed the course of her life.

Saint was married to director Jeffrey Hayden for 65 years until his death in 2016. She is survived by their two children, Darrell and Laurette, four grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.

Saint's death closes a remarkable chapter in the Golden Era of Hollywood history, leaving behind performances alongside some of the biggest and brightest stars and filmmakers of the 20th century.

item.title: Anthony Rizzo, 2016 World Series champion, reveals most important piece to winning it all in MLB postseason
item.description: Anthony Rizzo revealed the unsung heroes behind the Chicago Cubs' 2016 World Series run, and why Gary Sanchez is one for the Milwaukee Brewers.
item.content:encoded:
With the MLB postseason in full swing, every team and its fan base vying for the World Series trophy is hoping that their superstars can rise to the occasion and get the job done.

However, every great team who has hoisted the hardware at the end of a grueling season knows it takes more than just those All-Stars to win it all. In fact, it takes every single person from the top down.

Just ask World Series champion and three-time All-Star first baseman Anthony Rizzo, who helped the Chicago Cubs break its 108-year streak without winning a World Series in 2016 after defeating the Cleveland Guardians in Game 7.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Of course, it was stars like himself, Kris Bryant and others celebrating on the field after he secured the final out at first base. But Rizzo can’t help stressing the importance of every player, coach, clubhouse attendant and more during October baseball.

"I just think that on every team you have the stars, the middle-of-the-tier players, and your role players. Everyone’s so important to a team," Rizzo told OutKick, while highlighting PAYDAY’s "Low Key Legends" initiative, which emphasizes the importance of the unsung heroes within an organization. "It takes all 26 guys, it takes your entire staff. So, in order for the superstars to win their championship – let’s say Aaron Judge. He’s the MVP of the Yankees, of the whole league. For him to win a championship, it’s going to take every single guy on that roster. It’s not just one guy who carries you.

"It’s the small things. It’s the baserunning, the pickoffs, the relays. It’s all the lowkey things that maybe don’t look as glitzy and glammy, but that’s what it takes to win a championship."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

We asked Rizzo who his "Low Key Legend" would be, and he didn’t even hesitate when thinking back to his career.

"In the baseball world, I would definitely say Danny Mueller," he responded. "He was the clubhouse attendant in Chicago. He was my guy. He always had me high-energy, ready, and always a bundle of joy when I walked in. Whatever I needed, he was there. Then, the hitting coaches. They are just behind the scenes doing their scouting reports, knowing everything I’m thinking, so when I walk in, I don’t have to think. They just have everything ready for me, knowing what I want so I can go out there and play effortlessly.

"Those are the guys behind the scenes that are just fueling this greatness you see on the field."

At this stage of the season, teams have completely bonded into a family rather than just colleagues, if they didn’t do so during spring training and the early-season grind. Rizzo enjoyed every "family" he was a part of in the bigs, where October baseball brought out that team chemistry.

"I think we’re together forever. We’re together for 200-plus days a year," he said. "In October, win or go home, you’re still saying to each other, ‘In a few weeks, I get to pick my own friends.’ So, we’re like family in the clubhouse. Guys know when to get on guys, when they need a little more love, when to back off – maybe they’re a little more sensitive. That’s the family and bond that’s created in a season. Every year is different. Every year is unique, but for me over my career, Danny’s been a low-key legend for me forever, and my hitting coaches I’ve always had a good relationship with them where they always had my dialed in."

Then, when it’s time to play ball, it’s not just the clean-up hitter or the ace that carries the load of winning a postseason game. It takes a village, and the Milwaukee Brewers gave a prime example of that in Game 2 of their NLDS series against the San Diego Padres.

YANKEES' JAZZ CHISHOLM JR MAKES WILD ADMISSION ABOUT COSTLY ERROR AS TEAM FACES POSTSEASON ELIMINATION

Of course, the highlights will capture the moment Jackson Chourio walked it off in the bottom of the ninth inning with bases loaded and two outs against the Padres’ dominant closer, Mason Miller. That grabs the headlines and fan appreciation.

However, Rizzo pointed to an unsung hero – a "Low Key Legend" – that helped make it all possible.

"It’s a team of destiny because they’re a smaller market, but this is how they’ve been all year. To stay on brand with Payday and low-key legends, Gary Sanchez in the at-bat before, pinch hitting, taking the walk to get the bases loaded. That’s the low-key legend moment of the game. The superstar moment is when Jackson Chourio coming up and getting that base hit."

So, while your stars need to step up in the biggest ways possible in crucial moments throughout the postseason, always remember the "entire army" behind each franchise all battling for the same prize at the end of the year.

Those unsung heroes could be the difference between going home with nothing, or forever being called a champion.

item.title: Foreign adversaries running 'psyop' to fuel anti-AI and anti-data center movement, war official says
item.description: A Department of War official says foreign adversaries are running psyop campaigns to turn Americans against data centers and AI infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
A top official at the Department of War discussed how artificial intelligence is playing a role in war readiness strategy, and said foreign adversaries are carrying out "psyop" operations to fuel the anti-data center and anti-artificial intelligence movement across the U.S.

During an interview with Fox News Digital in the White House, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael warned that the movement to decrease production for artificial intelligence infrastructure is being pushed by America’s adversaries.

"It is natural from a propaganda standpoint that your adversary, who doesn't want you to be developing super intelligence ahead of them, is going to try to psyop your population into believing that. And to some degree, it's worked. And I think that's why you see the president push back and say, ‘no, this is a good thing,’" he said.

CRUZ SAYS WINNING AI RACE AGAINST CHINA IS 'SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ECONOMIC QUESTION' FOR AMERICA

Data center production has been at the center of debate ahead of the midterm elections, with lawmakers taking near-partisan stances as to whether developments should continue. Michael referred to data centers as the "electricity that fuels the superintelligence revolution," and explained that continued production of facilities are a crucial part of ensuring the U.S. maintains the lead in the artificial intelligence race.

Protests have popped up across the country against data centers and artificial intelligence advancements in general, with some lawmakers raising questions about the role that foreign influence plays in the demonstrations.

DATA CENTERS COULD BE THE SLEEPER ISSUE OF THE 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS

"It's the same reason we saw Middle Eastern countries paying for anti-fracking movements," Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital in an interview last month. "Because if they can convince America, 'Don't develop your oil and gas, just buy it from us,' well, that's great for them and terrible for us.

"The same is true on data centers. If they can convince Americans, 'You don't want data centers here, you want to just rely on the Chinese for AI,' that's great for China, and it's terrible for America."

CHINA ‘THROWING GASOLINE ON THE FIRE’ IN AI DATA CENTERS RACE, SAY LAWMAKERS

Michael echoed some of Cruz’s concerns about foreign influence, though he did not specifically name China as the culprit.

Lawmakers have raised questions about hundreds of millions of dollars that American-born communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham pumped into nonprofits and organizations that are now among the leading organizations fighting data center development throughout the country. Recipients of Singham's largesse include the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition, both self-described pro-China communist groups.

HOUSE PANEL TO PROBE FOREIGN ‘TROJAN HORSES’ AS SINGHAM SCRUTINY WIDENS

Last month, activists from both groups carried signs in a Chapel Hill, N.C., protest, merging anti-Trump sentiments with support for communist Cuba and opposition to data centers and AI development, including the message, "SHUT IT DOWN!"

Singham, a 72-year-old American who sold his tech company for $785 million in 2017 and now lives in Shanghai, is known to fund pro-Chinese Communist Party groups that operate in the U.S. He has funneled $278 million into the broad network of nonprofits since 2017, according to a Fox News Digital investigation.

MARXIST ORGANIZER LEADS CAMPAIGN AGAINST VIRGINIA AI DATA CENTER AS FOREIGN INFLUENCE CONCERNS MOUNT

The Party for Socialism and Liberation Boston, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit whose national chapter regularly partners with and supports the Singham network, posted to social media in July openly opposing data centers, saying the control of AI and data centers is in the hands of billionaires.

"Workers are rising up across the country in a growing movement against the tech billionaires – from fights against data centers in hundreds of cities, to labor organizing at the world’s biggest tech corporations," the post read.

As for how the Department of War utilizes artificial intelligence, Michael told Fox News Digital that usage has skyrocketed since Secretary Pete Hegseth assumed the cabinet role, growing from roughly 70,000 users out of a 3.5 million-person workforce to approximately 1.7 million today.

He explained that the Department of War is deploying artificial intelligence across three main areas: enterprise operations, warfighting and intelligence.

"We have incredible vignettes and stories about how people took 200 hours of work and combined it down to two hours," he added. "They can see what we have as assets. They can see what the adversary has as assets – they can time things better, they write quicker, they can consolidate orders quicker."

item.title: Nicole Scherzinger flashes abs in sports bra while revealing dangerous injury hidden from fans
item.description: Nicole Scherzinger shared photos of burns and blisters from boiling water that fell on her leg an hour before a Pussycat Dolls show in Düsseldorf.
item.content:encoded:
Nicole Scherzinger is showing fans what goes on behind the glamour.

The 48-year-old Pussycat Dolls singer led a new Instagram carousel with a polished backstage selfie, posing with her long dark hair styled in voluminous waves, glamorous makeup and her toned abs on display in a black sports bra and gray sweatpants.

But the next image told a very different story.

Scherzinger shared a close-up of her injured leg, revealing extensive red marks and healing burns stretching across the area around her knee and down her leg.

CÉLINE DION REVEALS 17-YEAR SECRET HEALTH BATTLE BEFORE RARE DIAGNOSIS

"What they see vs. what they don’t see..." she captioned the post.

CELINE DION BREAKS DOWN ONSTAGE DURING EMOTIONAL RETURN AFTER 6-YEAR HIATUS

The injury dates back to the Pussycat Dolls' Sept. 26 performance in Düsseldorf, Germany, when Scherzinger said boiling water fell on her leg approximately one hour before she was scheduled to take the stage.

Despite suffering burns and blisters, Scherzinger went ahead with the performance.

"Nothing like boiling water falling on your leg an hour before your set," she wrote on Instagram Stories at the time. "But the show must go on."

The singer's latest photos gave followers another look at the aftermath, contrasting the carefully put-together image audiences see backstage with the physical toll she has been managing behind the scenes.

Fans quickly praised Scherzinger for continuing to perform through the injury.

"How you continued to put on a show even after that! Incredible," one person wrote.

"You are truly the meaning of warrior Nicole Scherzinger," another commented.

Singer Gloria Gaynor also offered encouragement, writing, "you are a warrior, @nicolescherzinger!"

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Another follower called the injuries her "Battle scars."

Scherzinger has continued performing with the Pussycat Dolls throughout their "PCD Forever" tour, including a stop at Dublin's 3Arena on Oct. 5.

The current lineup features Scherzinger alongside Ashley Roberts and Kimberly Wyatt, who have reunited as a trio for the tour.

In Dublin, Scherzinger returned to the stage roughly a week after the accident, performing alongside Roberts and Wyatt as the group continued its European and U.K. run.

ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES

The tour continues Oct. 7 in Glasgow before moving through Newcastle and Manchester, with an Oct. 13 stop scheduled at London's O2 Arena.

Scherzinger's injury has been one of several challenges surrounding the group's latest reunion.

The "PCD Forever" tour marks the Pussycat Dolls' return to major arenas, but only three members of the group's best-known lineup are participating. Jessica Sutta, Carmit Bachar and Melody Thornton are not part of the current tour.

Sutta addressed the reunion in an exclusive video published on The Sun Tuesday, making clear that she has no interest in returning to her former role within the group.

"I'm not going to lip sync ‘Don’t Cha’ behind Nicole ever again," Sutta said in the clip.

Sutta said being left out of the reunion initially "broke my heart," though she also praised Scherzinger, Roberts and Wyatt for their performances.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I will say they need Carmit and Melody back as I think it’s better as a five," Sutta told the outlet. "But those three girls are killing it."

Sutta is currently focused on her solo career, with her new single, "Don't Take Much," set to be released Oct. 7.

item.title: Drone strike sinks ship in NATO waters as Zelenskyy warns of looming ‘massive strike’
item.description: A cargo ship sank and a second vessel caught fire in a combined aerial and maritime drone attack inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea.
item.content:encoded:
A commercial ship sank and its crew vanished Tuesday after an apparent coordinated air-and-sea drone attack off NATO member Bulgaria, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia before warning Moscow was preparing a broader "massive strike."

A second vessel was also heavily damaged and set ablaze inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, with a drone expert warning the dual precision strikes signaled a dangerous escalation and possible "larger invasion posture" by Russia.

"They were likely using the Geran-4 aerial drone to take the vessel out or the Maran surface vehicle to take it out," Cameron Chell, founder of drone manufacturer Draganfly, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday of the first strike.

RUSSIA MAY BE USING HIDDEN 'LUNCHBOX-SIZE' DRONE DEVICES TO COUNTER UKRAINE DEFENSES: EXPERT

"The reason it wasn't just an air vehicle or an air drone that took this ship out was that the Gerans generally come in at a pretty steep angle when they're on final attack," Chell said.

"There are not really any precision drones that fly closely above the surface, which is where they would have had to hit in order to create an impact that would sink this ship fast enough," he added.

"The nature of this strike suggests there was a combination of an air attack and surface attack," Chell said.

The dual attack occurred roughly 70 nautical miles off the eastern Bulgarian coastal town of Byala, according to Reuters, bringing the conflict into the economic zone of a NATO member.

Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence and security services were working to determine the full circumstances surrounding the attack.

US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS

"Our intelligence and special services are now working to establish all available information about yet another attack in the Black Sea targeting civilian vessels," he wrote on X.

"Our Navy contacted its counterparts in Bulgaria, and it has been established that this was a combined Russian attack using maritime and aerial drones."

Chell suggested the attack’s location and hybrid nature could serve Russia by sowing greater uncertainty across the region.

"We can see the amount of geopolitical chaos that's involved, and this is exactly the type of thing that would benefit Russia in the region," Chell said.

"The hybrid element here is really blurring the lines between traditional military actions," he added, describing the attack as "an expansion of strategy and tactics."

"This is indicative of this larger invasion posture that seems to be unfolding for Russia," Chell said. "And a real desire, what appears to be, for Russia to take things up a notch."

RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev also confirmed that aerial and maritime drones targeted two commercial vessels in shipping lanes inside Bulgaria’s EEZ, calling the attack a "gross, flagrant violation of international law," according to Reuters.

The sunken vessel, identified by British maritime risk group Vanguard as the cargo ship Alfa Watan, suffered catastrophic structural damage before submerging with an undisclosed cargo and an unknown number of crew members aboard.

A nearby Bulgarian ferry, the Dioscuria, diverted to the scene after witnessing an explosion and receiving distress signals, Reuters reported.

Rescuers found an overturned lifeboat, life rafts and life jackets floating in the debris field.

RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS

Search-and-rescue operations involving the Bulgarian Navy, Air Force and Border Police remained underway to locate the missing crew and monitor for environmental threats, the outlet said.

Chell suggested the apparent coordination between the attacks was particularly significant.

"Not only are you using pretty sophisticated equipment, but you're also doing it in a coordinated manner," Chell said.

"These two ships were going opposite directions. One was actually just coming, and had left Ukraine the day before," he said.

"These things coordinated and were struck relatively at the same time. So another level of coordination has unfolded here," Chell added.

UKRAINE POUNDS BLACK SEA FLEET’S ‘LAST MAJOR STRONGHOLD’ WHILE PUTIN FLEXES NAVAL POWER IN PACIFIC

The second ship, identified by Vanguard as the general cargo vessel ABLE, caught fire after being struck while carrying grain.

A Bulgarian ferry crew evacuated all 18 seafarers aboard — 11 Turkish nationals and seven Indian nationals.

Two crew members suffered severe injuries and were airlifted to a medical facility in Varna, while the remaining 16 were transported safely to shore.

Radev convened an emergency government session following the strikes. While acknowledging it remained unclear whether the drones originated from Russia or Ukraine, he warned of the widening scope of the war.

"Such an attack within the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable," Radev told reporters.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

"If this war is not ended in time, it will continue to expand its spatial scope and increase the risk of even a global conflict."

Chell said striking the two ships inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone could also have the effect of disrupting a crucial shipping corridor and creating fear among commercial operators.

"It all adds up to a perfect little scenario for the Russians to create chaos there, not just to disrupt the lane of economics for the region and in particular for Ukraine — a lifeline," Chell said.

"The Russians are really taking a playbook out of the Iranians who have basically created enough chaos in the Strait of Hormuz where the operators can't take the chance to put their ships through there," he added.

The strikes came amid a surge in attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea, including an incident off Romania’s coast Monday in which two people died in a ship fire.

Ambrey, a British firm specializing in global maritime risk, recorded more than 210 strikes on commercial ships between July and the end of September.

UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

Zelenskyy later warned that Ukrainian intelligence had obtained information indicating Russia was preparing a major new assault.

"We’ve got updated intel on Russia’s preparations for a massive strike," Zelenskyy wrote on X. "I ask you, please, to take care of yourselves and respond to missile threat alerts."

"Ukrainian services and our Air Force are ready to respond — as much as our defenses allow," Zelenskyy continued. "And a lot depends on our partners — every country in the world that has the defensive capabilities we need and can provide them to us."

"It’s very important that there be the political will to do this — particularly in the United States and in Europe," he added.

item.title: Urgent warning issued for island hot spot as State Department tells travelers to 'stay alert'
item.description: The U.S. State Department urges Americans to rethink travel to the popular island destination Djerba as the three-year anniversary of the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attack arrives.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. officials are warning Americans to steer clear of a popular tourist island on Wednesday, as heightened threats loom around the anniversary of the Oct. 7 terrorist attacks on Israel.

The U.S. Embassy in Tunisia issued the alert on Sunday concerning Djerba, a major tourist island off Tunisia's southern coast known for its white-sand beaches and resorts.

"Avoid travel to the island of Djerba on or around Oct. 7, 2026," the embassy said in a statement.

US WARNS AMERICANS TO STAY VIGILANT AS TERROR RISK LOOMS AT MAJOR VACATION HOT SPOT

Officials also asked Americans to avoid crowds and "stay alert and be aware of your surroundings."

"Avoid areas where there is a heavy police presence," the advisory said. "Monitor local media. Keep a low profile."

Wednesday marks the three-year anniversary of Oct. 7, 2023, when Hamas terrorists launched a major terrorist attack on Israel.

At the time, more than 1,200 people were killed and thousands more injured, beginning the Israel-Hamas war.

AMERICANS WARNED AGAIN TO RETHINK TRAVEL AS MISSILE ATTACK RATTLES HISTORIC REGION

The attack and ensuing war also fueled a rise in antisemitism worldwide, a potential concern in Djerba given the island's Jewish community.

Djerba, which became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023, has a long history of Jewish settlement dating back nearly 2,000 years, according to the World Jewish Congress.

Thousands of Jewish visitors from around the world travel to Djerba each year to celebrate the Lag B’Omer festival between Passover and Shavuot.

item.title: Veterans of 'unbearable' Chinese factory in Ohio detail brutal work conditions amid top Dem's oversight visit
item.description: Former Fuyao Glass America Inc. workers in Dayton, Ohio, described unbearable heat, union-busting tactics and a fatal accident to Rep. Ro Khanna.
item.content:encoded:
Former employees of Fuyao Glass America Inc., a Chinese-linked glass manufacturer that moved into an old General Motors plant in Ohio, gathered around one of the most prominent congressmen in the U.S. today to share their stories of misery, pain and neglect they claimed to have suffered while working for the CCP-linked corporation.

"My experience at Fuyao was not a good experience," Tiffany Moore, a woman who identified herself as a three-year veteran of the factory, told a group that gathered at the International Union of Electrical Workers in Dayton, Ohio, on Tuesday. 

"The heat in there is unbearable; they don’t care," she told the group — a group that included Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.

WHAT THE GOLF CART INDUSTRY CAN TEACH US ABOUT CHINA’S THREAT TO AMERICAN JOBS

Khanna, the ranking member on the House Select Subcommittee on the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), made the trek to Dayton to conduct Congressional oversight on Fuyao.

Khanna had previously sent Fuyao a letter asking them to submit a packet of information to his committee, including information on wage suppression, worker conditions and violating U.S. immigration and labor laws.

DEMAND TO END 'SCAM' VISA PROGRAM REPLACING AMERICAN WORKERS SURGES, WEST VIRGINIA CONGRESSMAN REVEALS

"Fuyao Glass America Inc. (FGA) has only provided a single supposed reply letter, dated September 23, that answers virtually none of the Committee’s questions in a material way and fails to include any document submissions," Khanna wrote in an Oct. 1 letter to the company’s leadership.

"Thus far, a generous interpretation of your approach toward this investigation would be that Fuyao does not appreciate Congress’s oversight function and the American system of government," Khanna wrote.

"A less generous interpretation of your lack of transparency would be that your companies have something to hide, beyond even what multiple federal investigations, documentaries, and press reports about Fuyao’s conduct have already uncovered," the letter, shared exclusively with Fox News Digital, read.

Khanna, despite requesting permission to visit the Lorraine, Ohio, factory, did not receive express permission from the company to do so. Despite the lack of response, Khanna continued to conduct his business, convening a roundtable that included a wide swath of former Fuyao workers.

BLUE STATES SET TO TRIGGER FRESH MINIMUM WAGE HIKES WITH PAY FLOORS MORE THAN DOUBLE FEDERAL RATE

Demetria Hodges, who identified herself as having worked at Fuyao for five years, explained how she believed the company went to great lengths to prevent the workers from unionizing.

"First they were trying to use scare tactics to get us to not vote for the union," Hodges said.

DAVID MARCUS: WHY JD VANCE'S RESHORING MESSAGE IS A PERFECT FIT FOR STRUGGLING SMALL TOWNS LIKE ST. CLOUD

"Then they offered a $2 an hour pay raise … which they have never given again. And that was like 10 years ago," she added.

An attendee named Darrell, who identified themselves as a former employee, also pointed out the company’s failure to cease operations when 57-year-old Ricky Patterson was killed in a grisly industrial accident in the factory.

item.title: Coyotes choose the front of a couple's Southern California cabin for an early morning scrap
item.description: Surveillance footage captured three coyotes brawling for 40 minutes outside a Southern California cabin in the San Bernardino Mountains area.
item.content:encoded:
The mystery surrounding why a couple's dog barks in the middle of the night at their Southern California cabin has been solved thanks to some early morning surveillance footage.

The footage revealed three coyotes right outside David and Annette Simpson's front door of their cabin in the San Bernardino Mountains. These wild animals weren't there to ask to borrow any sugar either.

They were there to fight. And fight they did for about 40 minutes, starting at around 1 a.m. Sunday morning.

The couple wasn't at home during the scrap in front of their cabin, but the action was caught on their surveillance cameras. What do you do with forty minutes of a coyote fight?

Well, naturally, you don't want it to go to waste, so you post it on social media, then sit down for an interview with the local news.

"We wonder why our dog barks in the middle of the night, and now we know," Annette Simpson told KTLA.

TWO MASSIVE ALASKAN BROWN BEARS FIGHT OVER PRIME FISHING SPOT AT LAKE CLARK NATIONAL PARK

Indeed. It must be due to those rambunctious coyotes. While nature doesn’t come calling at your door every day, a dog will certainly know when it does.

They've seen bears, squirrels and other wildlife before, but not a coyote scrap on the walkway in front of the cabin. That's a new one for these two.

Are they worried about how close the coyotes were to their cabin? Not Annette. She's into it.

"I think it’s pretty cool. We really enjoy watching the wildlife and just so close," she said. "Those stairs just lead right to our front door, and they came up those stairs."

item.content:encoded:
In the world’s "blue zones" — regions such as Sardinia, Italy, and Okinawa, Japan, known for unusually high concentrations of long-lived residents — researchers have studied dietary and lifestyle habits for clues to healthy aging and longevity.

In a recent video post, longevity researcher Dan Buettner highlighted three beverages commonly consumed in blue zones — and studies offer some clues about how each may affect health and longevity.

Buettner ranked water first among his three longevity drinks.

FILTERED WATER AT SPECIFIC AGES COULD ADD MONTHS TO YOUR LIFESPAN DECADES LATER, NEW STUDY FINDS

"The indisputable, best thing you can drink to live to 100 [is] water," he stated. "People in blue zones are drinking six to seven glasses of water. You want to make sure it is purified water. Water helps lower your blood pressure, helps keep your blood thin and keeps you hydrated."

Research from the National Institutes of Health has linked better hydration with healthier aging, including lower risks of chronic disease and premature death, although researchers noted that the findings do not prove cause and effect.

Other health experts note that adequate water intake supports kidney function, helps regulate blood pressure and keeps blood circulating effectively.

Coffee consumption is another daily habit highlighted by Buettner, who said it is associated with lower rates of diabetes and Parkinson's.

"Drink it black, one to two cups a day, quit by noon, it'll help you live longer," he added.

Coffee contains antioxidants and polyphenols, plant compounds that have been studied for their potential anti-inflammatory effects. Routine coffee consumption has also been associated with lower risks of type 2 diabetes and neurological conditions.

Limiting added sugars and heavy creams can help avoid extra calories, while consuming caffeine earlier in the day may reduce its impact on sleep.

Residents in blue zone areas, like Sardinia, often consume small amounts of red wine during meals.

Buettner acknowledged that red wine's place in a longevity-focused diet is "controversial."

"I'm very well aware of all the negative press wine is getting lately, but it's consumed in the blue zones and it seems to add years to life."

Red wine contains plant compounds such as resveratrol and flavonoids, which have been studied for their potential cardiovascular effects. However, experts have increasingly questioned whether any benefits attributed to red wine outweigh the known risks of alcohol.

item.title: Costco rolls out new Disneyland ticket deal but there's a catch for parkgoers
item.description: Costco's $329.99 Disneyland bundle includes a two-day Park Hopper ticket, Lightning Lane Multi Pass and a $60 dining card at select California stores.
item.content:encoded:
Disneyland visitors have a new ticket option that bundles park admission with other perks — but there are some restrictions that travelers may want to know about. 

Costco is offering a two-day Disneyland Resort Park Hopper ticket with Lightning Lane Multi Pass and a $60 dining card for $329.99 at select locations in California.

Disneyland Resort officials confirmed the offer to Fox News Digital, saying it rolled out last week at select Costco stores across the state.

DISNEYLAND CRACKS DOWN ON GUESTS WITH SWEEPING NEW RESTRICTIONS, SPARKING BACKLASH

The resort regularly makes limited-time ticket offers available throughout the year, including through third-party retailers, according to Disneyland Resort officials.

The Costco package has since caught the attention of theme park fans online as travelers compare the price with the cost of purchasing tickets directly from Disneyland.

In a recent Instagram post, one theme park content creator highlighted the $329.99 price and the included Lightning Lane access and dining card.

"Costco has a Disneyland deal right now that is actually WORTH talking about!" the user wrote.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

By comparison, a two-day Park Hopper ticket is currently listed at $445 for one adult on Disneyland's website, before adding Lightning Lane — though pricing is subject to change.

That puts the Costco package about $115 below the currently listed two-day Park Hopper price, although the two options come with different terms and restrictions.

The offer also comes as Disneyland adjusted some of its ticket prices this week. 

Mid-tier single-day tickets increased by $5, while the least expensive $104 ticket and the highest-priced $224 ticket remained unchanged, according to the Los Angeles Times.

The cost of Lightning Lane can now reach $38, up $1, while the Park Hopper add-on for single-day tickets increased by $5 to $10, depending on the date, the outlet reported. Multi-day ticket prices were unchanged.

Hugh Johnston, CFO of The Walt Disney Company, speaking at the recent Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference in San Francisco, said the company is keeping ticket prices accessible for younger families by offering lower rates during off-peak value periods.

"It's something that we're acutely sensitive to because we want to make sure we continue to bring young families, in particular, into the parks and develop that Disney love, right?" he said.

"So we're super sensitive to the fact that, particularly in the value times of the year, we keep those ticket prices relatively low so that we can actually encourage those young families to come in," he added.

The Costco ticket can be used between Oct. 2 and Dec. 18, according to information shared by the Instagram user.

Once a guest uses the ticket for the first time, the second park day must be used within 13 days, the video said.

Theme park reservations are also required for each visit, and the ticket is nonrefundable, according to the information shared online.

The same person must use both days of the ticket, meaning the two visits cannot be split between different travelers.

The offer is currently limited to select Costco locations in California, Disneyland Resort officials told Fox News Digital.

The package has generated mixed reactions among Disney fans online, with some questioning the cost of park visits and others praising the bundled price.

item.title: Iranian director decries Hollywood portrayal of foreign countries, calls American democracy 'a lie'
item.description: Director Asghar Farhadi slammed Ben Affleck's "Argo" at the Rio Film Festival, calling it a "Hollywood thing" that portrays Iran "like you're in hell."
item.content:encoded:
Oscar-winning Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi called out Hollywood's depiction of Iran and other foreign countries at the Rio Film Festival in Brazil on Friday, claiming it is a "lie" to call America a "democracy."

While promoting his film "Parallel Tales," Farhadi was asked about the 2012 movie "Argo" winning Best Picture just one year after his film "A Separation" won Best Foreign Language Film at the Oscars. 

"Argo," directed by Ben Affleck, stars Affleck as CIA operative Tony Mendez in a loose adaptation of Mendez's memoir on the rescue of six U.S. diplomats from Iran by pretending to film a science-fiction movie in the nation.

BEN AFFLECK REJECTS 'PROPAGANDA' OPPOSING AI, INSISTS EMERGING TECHNOLOGY WILL HELP FILMMAKERS

Farhadi described the film as a "Hollywood thing" and suggested it was "not deep" based on its plot involving a "White guy" saving others, though Mendez in real life was of Mexican descent.

"They make these movies for money; it’s a business," Farhadi said, according to Variety. "And in these films it’s always a [W]hite guy from the United States saving others. My question is: Why? Why does an American go to Cuba or Iran to save people? People understand they can save themselves. Who asked you to come and save us?"

Farhadi also accused "Argo," which took place after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, of portraying Iran "like you're in hell."

AMERICAN WHO FLED IRAN SAYS CITIZENS 'DESPERATE' FOR FREEDOM, PRAYING FOR ISLAMIC REGIME TO FALL

"The problem with these kinds of films in Hollywood [and] some people in the United States [is that] they look at the world from up to down," Farhadi said. "Someday you should ask them: Why do you feel you’re up and we’re down? I don’t understand why they have this ego that they’re up."

Farhadi also denied Americans' claim to "have democracy," saying he believed the "real America" exists among Black and foreign prisoners.

"You don’t have democracy. It’s a lie," Farhadi said.

VICTOR DAVIS HANSON DISSECTS HOW CRITICS COMPLETELY MISREAD THE IRAN DEAL

Fox News Digital reached out to Farhadi's and Affleck's representatives for comment.

Media Research Center President David Bozell called out Farhadi's negative view of America and American films in a comment to Fox News Digital.

"America was asked to save the world, and we did, not once, but twice. And we’re always preparing to do it again, if we’re asked to, at a moment’s notice. Maybe Hollywood makes movies about Americans saving the world for a reason," Bozell said.

item.title: Miami Hurricanes coach comes out in favor of ending preseason college football polls, blasts SEC
item.description: Shannon Dawson calls preseason rankings "the stupidest thing on the planet" and argues SEC teams get undeserved benefit of the doubt from voters.
item.content:encoded:
There may not be a better season than 2026 to exemplify the problems with preseason polls in college football.

The advent of NIL and the transfer portal has already made gauging the "best" teams in early August nearly impossible, and as the jaw-dropping 2025 Indiana Hoosiers championship season demonstrated, the modern era has created more surprise teams than in the past.

Preseason polls then, despite being a part of the college football process for years, are less useful than ever before. And one prominent offensive coordinator thinks we should get rid of them entirely. He's probably right.

Miami Hurricanes OC Shannon Dawson recently addressed the preseason polls, specifically addressing how they consistently seemingly favor one specific conference. A conference that already more often than not gets the benefit of the doubt from poll voters.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"First of all, there should be no such thing as preseason rankings," Dawson said during a press conference. "That’s the most ridiculous thing on the planet. That is the stupidest thing, because people weigh those things way heavier than they should.

"You shouldn’t have a ranking until October. How do you know? (Texas) A&M was ranked in the top-five, but how does that look right now? If anything, it isn’t predictable for the future, it’s the past. Go look at the top-10 last year. I did. Five of them weren’t even in the (end of season) top-25."

It's impossible to argue with that, because it's true. And despite A&M, and others, looking far worse than their preseason expectations, the first few weeks of games and rankings reflect that initial set. Texas A&M loses to LSU, which must mean LSU is good, because A&M was a preseason top-5 team. Missouri was ranked in the preseason, for some reason, which must mean Mississippi State is also good, because they beat a preseason top-25 team.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Obviously the preseason poll doesn't only affect one conference; Big Ten teams like Michigan, Penn State and Washington have looked far worse than preseason polls suggested. On the other hand, though, Nebraska and Wake Forest have received little attention and respect from voters, despite deserving it, because they didn't start the year in the top-25.

Dawson continued, specifically calling out the SEC and how those teams fluctuate from week-to-week.

"So we sit here and look at schedules, and obviously everything is SEC, SEC. Well look… they have all of their teams in the top-25. Guess what. Good for you. At the end of the year, half of them won’t be in the top-30. That’s just the way it is. We can’t sit here and say, ‘hey, we play X number of top-25 teams’. We don’t know that. We’ll count those chips up at the end of the year.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"That’s why there shouldn’t be rankings, because you give people talking points that are idiots. They don’t know what they’re doing. Play the game. Play every week."

It's like Dawson's been reading a certain OutKick writer's columns complaining about the polls each week. Ahem.

Voters are humans, and humans are biased. They don't always watch all the games, and some have even forgotten to rank elite teams like Miami periodically. Some, like ESPN's Heather Dinich, post about the importance of winning "SEC road games," as if that some sort of remarkable achievement. Her specific example, Kentucky, beat a bad Texas A&M team and a bad South Carolina team. Great, so what? Why should that be rewarded by placing the Wildcats at No. 17, just because it's the SEC and those teams have big stadiums?

At the end of the day, using a blend of analytics and efficiency driven rankings would lead to a better result than trusting voters. Especially before anyone's even seen teams play on the field. But because there are vested interests who want preseason polls to continue, they will. Many valuable college football traditions have gone by the wayside in the modern game, but somehow not that one.

item.title: Transgender Washington state resident accused of fueling deadly Canadian school massacre that killed 8: DOJ
item.description: James Cody Bryant allegedly sent money, offered advice and agreed to livestream the Tumbler Ridge school shooting instead of alerting law enforcement.
item.content:encoded:
A transgender Washington state resident allegedly helped fuel a Canadian school massacre that left children dead, choosing to aid the shooter, who also identified as a transgender, instead of sounding the alarm, federal officials said Tuesday.

James Cody Bryant, 30, was arrested Tuesday morning in Bellingham north of Seattle, accused of sending money, offering advice and agreeing to broadcast the Feb. 10 attack at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia.

"Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement, and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to," Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said at a Seattle news conference.

"Instead, he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer."

TRANSGEDNER EX-STUDENT IDENTIFIED AS ALLEGED SUSPECT IN DEADLY CANADA SCHOOL MASS SHOOTING

Bryant faces a federal charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Prosecutors allege Bryant helped the shooter, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, start a car to reach the school after the killings had begun.

"So even after the shooter had already tragically killed two family members, Bryant assisted the shooter in successfully traveling to the second location to take even more lives," FBI Seattle Special Agent in Charge W. Mike Herrington said.

"In the complaint, Bryant even admits to being maybe the only one who could stop the shooter."

Herrington confirmed that Bryant and Van Rootselaar both identified as transgender, and said Bryant identifies as female.

The two met through a random pairing on the online chat service Omegle roughly three years before the attack. 

Investigators have no indication what their transgender identities were, why they remained in contact, or that they ever met in person, Herrington said.

TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL

Their online friendship developed into discussions of violence over at least six months, according to Herrington.

"This complaint was particularly difficult to read, in part because of the casual tone these two individuals used when discussing the mass taking of innocent lives that was being planned," he said.

Bryant allegedly agreed to record and broadcast a livestream to maximize the shooter’s notoriety.

"Bryant even stayed awake after an overnight work shift to make sure this horrific act could be widely viewed online," Herrington said.

FLORIDA MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY PLOTTING MASS SHOOTING TARGETING JEWISH EMPLOYEES AT ADVOCACY ORGANIZATION

"We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the livestream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the livestream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

Floyd said the attempted livestream on Twitch lasted about 20 seconds before shutting down. Herrington said investigators do not know whether Van Rootselaar would have carried out the attack without Bryant’s willingness to operate it.

Officials also described financial assistance, including a little more than $100 for shoes. An attempted transfer of roughly $15 for a lighter was ultimately reversed.

NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

Floyd said Bryant and the shooter discussed sending weapons to Canada, but Bryant was uncomfortable doing so. Herrington said investigators had no indication the guns used in the attack came from the U.S.

Asked about a possible political ideology or group affiliation, Floyd said investigators had no information indicating either.

Herrington pointed to the shooter’s suffering and "a very keen focus on notoriety" as themes in the communications. The pair discussed other mass shootings, how the public reacted and a desire for the Tumbler Ridge attack to receive similar attention, he said.

The investigation crossed the border within days of the massacre, when Canadian police received information from an online platform used by the shooter and contacted the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), British Columbia RCMP Assistant Commissioner Elija Rain said.

Floyd said investigators obtained subpoenas and warrants and reviewed thousands of communications, many on Discord, before making the arrest.

Canadian investigators have reviewed more than 90 statements from students, educators and first responders and continue to examine other online contacts, Rain said.

GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT COLT GRAY CHANGES PLEA TO GUILTY, NOW FACES LIFE IN PRISON

"Our RCMP criminal investigation remains ongoing and the possibility of further charges being pursued in Canada remains under active consideration," he said.

Herrington warned that assisting a mass shooting from afar does not shield someone from prosecution.

"If you think you are safe from prosecution because you did not pull the trigger, or were not physically present at the scene of the crime, think again," he said.

"The FBI and our partners will use all of the considerable investigative tools at our disposal to hold accountable those who enable or assist in acts of mass violence."

The Feb. 10 attack killed eight victims, including five students, an educator and the shooter’s mother and 11-year-old stepbrother, according to Canadian authorities. Van Rootselaar was found dead inside the school from an apparent self-inflicted injury.

item.title: Unearthed social media posts contradict El-Sayed’s ‘capitalist’ narrative
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic U.S. Senate candidate in Michigan, faces scrutiny over Detroit DSA ties as he prepares to face Mike Rogers.
item.content:encoded:
Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, recently embraced the "capitalist" label and pushed back against being called socialist, but unearthed social media posts contradict that narrative.

Recently unearthed social media posts show the Detroit Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) chapter applauding his views on climate advocacy, going so far as to call him a "comrade" in its efforts.

"Welcome to the team comrade," the group’s Detroit chapter wrote in a post in 2019 alongside a picture of El-Sayed, then a recent candidate for Michigan governor.

Shortly after El-Sayed endorsed Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., in his presidential bid, the account again praised his support.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ENDORSED BY AOC AND BERNIE SANDERS INSISTS HE'S NOT A SOCIALIST

"Thank you to our friend and ally Abdul El-Sayed for endorsing Bernie Sanders. Our movement is unstoppable," the group wrote.

Although the DSA has not officially endorsed El-Sayed in his Senate bid or affirmed his platform, the DSA’s local support for him may raise questions of increased overlap between his platform and the DSA's official stances.

In an interview with The New York Times, El-Sayed described his views on capitalism.

"Capitalism is about leveraging the laws of supply and demand to efficiently allocate capital expenditure to maximize value. When capitalism works, it’s because you have free entry and exit into markets," El-Sayed said.

"So if you believe in capitalism, you have to believe in government regulation to protect markets. In fact, right now, we have exactly the opposite. You don’t have to be a socialist to believe that you should be taxing billionaires their wealth," he continued. "In fact, if you are a capitalist, you should believe in that. So, I’m a capitalist who just knows about capitalism. I have a bad habit of reading; I’m so sorry."

Among other stances, El-Sayed has championed policies like Medicare for All, increasing taxes on the country’s top earners and implementing more stringent penalties on businesses that, in his view, abuse natural resources like water supply and air quality.

In his 2018 campaign for governor, El-Sayed espoused many of the same views, garnering support from the DSA — especially for his platform on climate.

At one point, El-Sayed joined in calls to seize plants owned by General Motors after the company announced it would cut about 14,000 jobs from sites across the country.

GREEN NEW DODGE: EL-SAYED RUNS FROM POLICY AS NEWLY SURFACED DELETED POSTS SHOW YEARS OF SUPPORT

"Today, Abdul El-Sayed signed onto our bold demand to seize abandoned [General Motors] plants and convert them into green, public use. This is the courage and vision we need from our leaders to make the Green New Deal a reality. Thank you, Dr. El-Sayed! Onward!" The group wrote.

El-Sayed was among 140 co-signers for the plan, including figures like Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., and Natasha Fernández-Silber, the co-chair of the Detroit DSA.

"These facilities are not just the ‘property’ of a corporation. They belong to the workers who have contributed their labor, and the taxpayers who have provided enormous tax breaks, public subsidies and bailouts to GM," the resolution read.

Between 2017 and 2020, the Michigan Democrat spoke at six events held by Democratic Socialists of America chapters, including a 2019 fundraiser where he served as the keynote speaker. Additionally, DSA officials told Politico in July that they were mobilizing resources to help El-Sayed win his Democratic primary election.

"I'm not technically or practically DSA," El-Sayed told the Wall Street Journal in July.

Socialist organizers, however, have called him "a longtime friend of Detroit DSA."

"Our annual fundraiser is going to be [fire] this year. Chaired by the one and only Rashida Tlaib, with guest speaker Abdul El-Sayed," another post reads.

"Our annual Douglas-Debs Dinner is THIS SATURDAY! The one and only Rashida Tlaib will give the keynote, with special guest speaker Abdul El-Sayed. Don’t miss out. Get your tickets today!" another stated.

For its own part, the national platform for the DSA goes well beyond the proposals that El-Sayed has made a part of his Senate bid.

JONATHAN TURLEY: ABDUL EL-SAYED’S WEALTH-TAX FANTASY COULD WRECK THE MICHIGAN ECONOMY

Among other positions, the group has championed abolishing the U.S. Senate, establishing public ownership of the country’s largest corporations and defunding the Department of Defense — stances that El-Sayed has not voiced support for.

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether El-Sayed believes the past support from the Detroit DSA undermines his claims about what he believes about capitalism.

Having cleared the Democratic primary, El-Sayed will face off against Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers on Nov. 3.

Fox News' Robert Schmad contributed to this report

item.title: ‘Digger’ bombs: A rare box-office misfire for Tom Cruise
item.description: Tom Cruise's dark comedy "Digger" earned just $8 million domestically despite a reported budget of up to $150 million, marking a rare career low.
item.content:encoded:
You can’t win ’em all.

That’s a phrase Hollywood’s global cinematic icon and producer Tom Cruise isn’t likely to hear often. But this past weekend, what many consider Hollywood’s biggest movie star in history suffered one of the worst debuts of his career. The painful performance at the box office of the dark comedy "Digger" was one for the headlines.

Cruise earned legendary praise for keeping Paramount’s "Top Gun: Maverick" out of streaming services during the pandemic, forcing a theatrical-only release that grossed $1.5 billion worldwide, and has long been viewed as the studio’s "golden boy," anchoring multibillion-dollar intellectual properties and protecting the traditional theatrical experience.

TOM CRUISE UNVEILS DRAMATIC TRANSFORMATION IN FIRST LOOK AT ALEJANDRO IÑÁRRITU’S HIGHLY-ANTICIPATED 'DIGGER'

The Alejandro G. Iñárritu-directed "Digger," however, delivered a disappointing farewell note for Warner Bros. as a standalone studio.

It grossed only $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally, where Cruise is ordinarily a big draw. That’s despite the film reportedly costing between $125 million and $150 million to make, with marketing expenses estimated at $100 million.

"Given his extraordinary history with Paramount, the timing certainly adds an interesting layer to the story, but one movie doesn’t erase decades of success or the value he brings to a studio," Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends for global media measurement and data analytics company Rentrak, told Fox News Digital. "There are lessons to be learned from ‘Digger,’ particularly around budget, positioning and expectations, but I don’t see this changing the fact that studios will continue to want to work with him."

Meanwhile, the weekend’s No. 1 box office draw, debuting with $32.6 million, went to Amazon MGM’s erotic psychological thriller "Verity," directed by Michael Showalter and starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett. The film’s strong showing extends a winning streak for adaptations of author Colleen Hoover’s work at the box office.

SAUDI-BACKED 'DESERT WARRIOR' GROSSES JUST $472K ON A $150M BUDGET IN HISTORIC BOX OFFICE DISASTER

Following "Verity," Zach Cregger’s video game adaptation "Resident Evil" came in second for Sony Pictures with $12.5 million, while Paramount’s "Heart of the Beast," starring Brad Pitt as a former special forces soldier trapped in the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog, grossed $11 million. That was followed by director Lance Oppenheim’s "Primetime" and "Digger."

In the case of "Digger," critics weren’t especially kind, with the film earning a 51% score on Rotten Tomatoes. Cruise pulled out all the stops, giving a rare one-on-one interview with GQ magazine as part of the promotional campaign for the climate satire.

The film’s London premiere on Sept. 22 at the ODEON Luxe Leicester Square brought out Prince William and Princess Catherine, as the event also served as this year’s royal charity screening benefiting the UK’s Film and TV Charity. While Cruise welcomed the two on the red carpet, David Beckham also made an appearance with his two sons, Cruz and Romeo.

TOM CRUISE ADMITS RUMORS ABOUT HIS 'INTENSE' BEHAVIOR ON MOVIE SETS ARE TRUE

The underwhelming opening comes as Paramount Skydance closes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in a $110 billion deal.

Despite "Digger’s" poor showing, Dergarabedian said it won’t ultimately affect Cruise as a Hollywood powerhouse.

"I think the interesting thing here is that the result really doesn’t change the fundamental reality that every studio wants to be in the Tom Cruise business," he said. "‘Digger’ was always a much tougher commercial proposition than the kind of broad, action-driven, franchise-oriented films audiences traditionally associate with Cruise." 

"The challenge was that having Tom Cruise as the star didn’t automatically make it a Tom Cruise blockbuster, nor was the movie necessarily designed to be one," Dergarabedian added.

item.title: American-born Canada soccer coach Jesse Marsch takes aim at home country before USMNT friendly
item.description: Jesse Marsch called America a propaganda-infused nation ahead of the USMNT friendly, claiming the rest of the world hates Americans overseas.
item.content:encoded:
Jesse Marsch was born in Wisconsin, played professionally in MLS and represented the United States as both a player and an assistant coach before landing premier managerial jobs in Europe and eventually taking over the Canadian national team in 2024.

The case could quite easily be made that Marsch owes a significant amount of his career to being born in the United States. After all, he played collegiately at Princeton under coach Bob Bradley before being drafted by D.C. United in 1996. When Marsch retired from playing, Bradley happened to be the coach of the U.S. men's national team. Marsch joined his staff, and his coaching career was off and running.

Marsch lived the American soccer dream in a time when one didn't even really exist, but seems to have lost any form of appreciation for that. Who knows, he may have never had any to begin with.

Marsch's Canadian side is set to take on the U.S. men's national team in a friendly on Tuesday in Saint Paul, Minnesota. In the days leading up to the match, the 52-year-old chose to stoke the fires by explaining that his home country is nothing but a propaganda-infused nation hated by the rest of the world.

"We, as Americans, have been inundated with propaganda since we were young," Marsch told The Guardian in a piece published on Oct. 4. "We’re the No 1 country in the world, we deserve everything, we dominate everything, No 1 in every aspect of life. This is what we’ve been told. So, when things happen and we don’t feel like we’re in control of it … we feel like we deserve to be treated differently because we’re Americans.

That is one of the things that infuriates the rest of the world about Americans. And Americans don’t know that if they don’t ever leave the country."

Talking about America as if it's North Korea and insinuating that Americans who never travel the world have no sense of reality is bold, but something Marsch clearly feels strongly about, considering he delivered the comments after being asked about U.S. forward Folarin Balogun having a red card rescinded during this summer's World Cup.

"So what I feel when the Balogun ruling happens is that would never happen in any other country in the world, and this is why everyone around the world hates America," Marsch continued.

"That was proven to be so. The U.S. had a good World Cup, was doing well. All that switched in one moment. But do I think that that’s about corruption and unfairness? The problem is, football is inundated with this kind of stuff."

Marsch's claims of the sport of soccer as a whole being filled with corruption ring true, but the rest of his thoughts feel deeply rooted in the current political climate in the United States.

That's because they are.

Speaking with reporters on Monday to preview the friendly, Marsch was asked if he feels more American or Canadian. After admitting he was American but "honored and really proud" to be Canada's national team coach, he stated that he believes he has a "unique perspective" on things.

His unique perspective seems to only offer a negative outlook on his home country.

"Here we are now, the big talk in America is Lake Ontario, Lake America, this kind of crap," Marsch said, referring to President Donald Trump's executive order for renaming Lake Ontario.

"There’s a uniqueness to Canada in terms of how truly multiethnic this country has become," Marsch continued. "You can see that Canada is not just a North American country anymore, you know? That bodes well for our sport and for the makeup of our team, the makeup of our fans."

Despite Canada's open border policies and Marsch's outlook on the country, Canada is, in fact, just another North American country.

Marsch is 17-14-7 as Canada's manager, but if he keeps bad-mouthing his new country's neighbor to the south and pushing liberal talking points during press conferences, his mediocre record will be overlooked for quite some time.

item.title: Caitlin Clark's lowest-rated playoff game still outdrew every non-Fever first-round broadcast
item.description: Indiana Fever averaged nearly twice the viewers of non-Fever games, with Caitlin Clark's streaming audience topping traditional TV broadcasts.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark's least-watched playoff game this year still drew a bigger audience than every non-Fever first-round game.

And it was the one fans needed Prime Video to watch.

Indiana's Sept. 29 win over the Las Vegas Aces averaged 1.42 million viewers on Amazon's streaming service, according to Sports Media Watch. The largest audience for a first-round game without the Fever was 1.40 million for Golden State's Game 2 loss to Dallas on ESPN.

KELSEY MITCHELL’S CAITLIN CLARK COMMENTS DESERVE CONTEXT, INCLUDING THE BENEFITS OF ALL THAT ATTENTION

The difference was small, approximately 20,000 viewers. But Clark's lowest number came on a streaming-exclusive broadcast and still finished ahead of every non-Fever audience, including those that aired on network television and cable.

Two nights later, Indiana's season-ending loss to Las Vegas averaged 2.25 million viewers across USA Network and CNBC, making it the second-most-watched WNBA first-round playoff game ever.

Can you guess who played in the most-watched first-round game ever? Yeah, it was Clark and the Fever against the Connecticut Sun in 2024, which saw Game 2 of their first-round series average 2.54 million viewers on ESPN.

So, across three games, Clark helped deliver one of the biggest first-round audiences in league history and a streaming audience that exceeded every non-Fever telecast. 

That's a pretty good illustration of what she means to the WNBA.

Indiana's three games averaged approximately 1.93 million viewers, compared with 985,000 for the seven non-Fever games. That gave Clark's games an average audience approximately 96% larger than the other first-round games, nearly double the audience.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And while networks, start times and streaming distribution varied across all those games, the opening Sunday offered a very clean comparison point.

ABC aired New York–Minnesota and Indiana–Las Vegas on Sept. 27. The Liberty–Lynx opener averaged 1.20 million viewers while the Fever–Aces opener averaged 2.11 million.

Same day. Same network. Approximately 76% more viewers for the Fever.

There's also a comparison within Prime Video. Washington–Atlanta's opener averaged 425,000 viewers.

Angel Reese, who now plays for Atlanta, famously insisted in 2024 that people watch women's basketball "because of me too." But on the same streaming platform, Clark's Fever drew more than three times the audience of Reese's Dream.

Last year, I wrote about the Fever's playoff opener without an injured Clark. Indiana drew 951,000 viewers on ABC, compared with 1.84 million for its opener with Clark the previous year. Both games aired in the same Sunday afternoon slot opposite the NFL.

The 2025 All-Star Game offered another example. With Clark sidelined, ABC averaged 2.19 million viewers, down from roughly 3.4 million in 2024.

Then, with Clark back in 2026, the number jumped back over 3 million.

There is also evidence that fans will watch the league after Indiana is eliminated. In 2024, I noted that the semifinals were delivering strong audiences, including Liberty–Aces games that outdrew every game of those teams' championship series the year before.

For the WNBA, the opportunity is to turn fans who arrive for Clark into fans who stay for everybody else. These numbers show there is a long way to go in that department.

The two Fever games on traditional television each drew more than two million viewers. Even Indiana's streaming-exclusive game edged the biggest reported non-Fever telecast. The seven non-Fever games averaged under one million viewers.

The remaining teams now have a chance to make their own case to viewers, with a championship still to be decided. I'll be interested to see those audiences when they're available.

The WNBA's biggest draw is done for the season. Now we find out how many viewers are.

item.title: Michael Douglas admits he almost left his wife for his 'Basic Instinct' co-star after affair
item.description: Michael Douglas reveals in his memoir "One Helluva Ride" that he had affairs with his "Basic Instint" co-star and Kathleen Turner on set of hit films.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Douglas is letting go of all his secrets in his new memoir.

According to Page Six, the 82-year-old actor disclosed in his new book, "One Helluva Ride, that he had an affair with a co-star almost 20 years his junior while filming the 1992 movie, "Basic Instinct."

While many at the time believed Douglas and his on-screen love interest, Sharon Stone, were having an affair in real life, the actor admitted in the memoir that it was actually actress Jeanne Tripplehorn with whom he was having the affair.

"The truth is, I fell very hard for Jeanne despite our nearly 20-year age difference," he said in the book. "In fact, I was ready to officially leave my wife for Jeanne. I was crazy about her."

MICHAEL DOUGLAS CONFIRMS SECRET AFFAIR WITH KATHLEEN TURNER ON 'ROMANCING THE STONE' SET

At the time, Douglas was still married to his first wife, Diandra Luker, although he has said they were separated and living separate lives. Luker eventually filed for divorce in 1995.

He went on to say that his "relationship with Jeanne lasted through production," but that they "went our separate ways" once they were done making the film.

"But I will always think of her as an amazing actress and a truly terrific woman that I was very fortunate to spend time with," he added.

"Basic Instinct" follows Douglas' character, homicide detective Nick Curran, as he is seduced by a crime novelist and prime murder suspect, played by Sharon Stone. Tripplehorn portrayed police psychologist Dr. Beth Garner, who was also Curran's lover.

Elsewhere in the book, the "Wall Street" actor admitted to engaging in an affair with Kathleen Turner when they worked together on the 1984 movie, "Romancing the Stone."

"The truth is that during the production of Romancing the Stone, Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship," he wrote in an excerpt obtained by People. "It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen."

He wrote that when he left home to film the movie, he and Luker were "still technically married, but separated," and that while audiences were "certain for years that we were in a relationship together" while making the movie, they denied it, even through the making of the sequel and years later when they reunited on "The Kominsky Method."

item.title: Christa Pike now conscious and talking after surviving 2 doses of lethal injection drug
item.description: Christa Pike is awake and talking after surviving two doses of pentobarbital during Tennessee's failed execution attempt, her attorneys say.
item.content:encoded:
A Tennessee death row inmate is awake and talking after surviving two doses of a lethal injection drug during a failed execution, her attorneys said Tuesday.

Christa Pike continues to receive critical medical care following Tennessee’s attempt to execute her last Wednesday, her attorneys said in a statement posted on the Mercy for Christa website.

"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," the statement said.

They said Pike remains handcuffed and shackled to her hospital bed despite severe damage to her arms.

LAWYERS, EXPERTS URGE TENNESSEE GOVERNOR TO COMMUTE CHRISTA PIKE’S SENTENCE AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

"Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery," the statement said.

Her attorneys said Pike survived two complete rounds of lethal injection under Tennessee’s protocol despite their warnings about problems with her veins. They thanked first responders and hospital staff for her care and renewed their request for Tennessee’s governor to commute her sentence to life without parole.

Pike, now 50, was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at the Knoxville Job Corps Center.

LETHAL INJECTION SURVIVOR CHRISTA PIKE'S FORMER SATANIST BOYFRIEND COULD BE RELEASED IN 5 YEARS

Pike was 18 when she and two classmates lured Slemmer to a park, where they tortured her for nearly an hour before crushing her skull with a chunk of broken asphalt, former Knoxville Police Chief Phil Keith previously told Fox News Digital.

Pike kept a fragment of Slemmer’s skull as a trophy and showed it to classmates before her arrest.

TENNESSEE PRISON CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER FAILED EXECUTION AS FORMER US ATTORNEY TAPPED TO LEAD INDEPENDENT REVIEW

Pike is the first person in the modern U.S. death penalty era known to survive the administration of lethal injection drugs, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Pike’s attorneys have also filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence from the failed execution attempt. They plan to hold a press conference Wednesday following a Davidson County Chancery Court hearing scheduled to begin at 11 a.m. local time.
